Show it only as light, cloud, fire or radiance where the scene plan places it. No figure, face, hands, robe, hair or seated shape, even made of light.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady in bearing; olive skin weathered by travel; dark hair and a short, neatly kept beard with some early grey; a grave, resolute face with deep-set dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak fastened at the shoulder, with a governor's embroidered band of red and gold at the hem. Carries alone a bronze signet ring on his right hand.
- Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.
- the priests consulted in Haggai: a typical member is a man in middle age, lean and dignified, with a weathered brown skin, closely trimmed dark beard and short dark hair beneath a plain white linen turban. His signature outfit is a long white linen priestly tunic with a dark blue woven sash, worn over a plain undergarment.
- Only Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple), the priests consulted in Haggai have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.
